ramayana-6-11-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-12.translation: "With many reasons and words I showed him again and again: 'Let Sita be properly returned to Rama.'"
ramayana-6-11-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-13.translation: "But Ravana, driven by fate, did not accept the good words spoken to him, like a dying man refusing medicine."
ramayana-6-11-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-14.translation: "Spoken to harshly by him and insulted like a slave, I have left my sons and wives and come to Raghava for refuge."
ramayana-6-11-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-15.translation: "Tell great Raghava, refuge of all the worlds, quickly that I, Vibhishana, have come."
ramayana-6-11-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-16.translation: Hearing these words, swift Sugriva, agitated, spoke to Rama in front of Lakshmana.
ramayana-6-11-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-17.translation: "Ravana's younger brother, known as Vibhishana, has come to you for refuge with four rakshasas."
ramayana-6-11-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-18.translation: "Know that Vibhishana has been sent by Ravana. I think it right to seize him, best of the patient."
ramayana-6-11-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-19.translation: "This rakshasa has come with crooked intent, sent to strike, hidden by illusion, when you trust him, Raghava."
ramayana-6-11-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-20.translation: "Let him be punished severely with his ministers, for this Vibhishana is the brother of cruel Ravana."
ramayana-6-11-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-21.translation: Having said this to Rama, the agitated army commander, skilled in speech, fell silent before the eloquent one.
ramayana-6-11-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-22.translation: Hearing Sugriva's words, mighty Rama spoke to the monkeys near him, led by Hanuman.
ramayana-6-11-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-23.translation: "You too have heard the very reasoned words the monkey king has spoken about Ravana's younger brother."
ramayana-6-11-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-24.translation: "In times of difficulty a wise, good and able friend, who wishes lasting good, should give counsel."
ramayana-6-11-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-25.translation: Asked thus, they eagerly gave their own views to Rama, with courtesy, wishing his good.
ramayana-6-11-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-26.translation: "There is nothing in the three worlds unknown to you, Raghava. You ask us out of friendship, honouring us, Rama."
ramayana-6-11-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-27.translation: "You are true to your vows, brave, righteous, firm in valour, acting after testing, thoughtful, and you open yourself to your friends."
ramayana-6-11-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-28.translation: "So let your counsellors speak one by one, wise and able, giving reasons again and again."
ramayana-6-11-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Vibhishana arrives and asks Rama for refuge; Sugriva suspects him, and Rama asks his counsellors' views.

ramayana-6-11-29.translation: When this was said, wise Angada, the monkey, spoke first to Raghava, to test Vibhishana.
ramayana-6-11-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-30.translation: "Coming from the enemy, he must surely be suspected in every way. Vibhishana should not be trusted hastily."
ramayana-6-11-30.meaning: Be cautious with one from the enemy camp.
ramayana-6-11-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-31.translation: "The deceitful move about hiding their true nature, and strike at weak points; that would be a great disaster."
ramayana-6-11-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-32.translation: "After weighing good and harm, one should decide: accept him for his merits, reject him for his faults."
ramayana-6-11-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-33.translation: "If there is great fault in him, let him be rejected without hesitation; or if many merits are known, let him be accepted, king."
ramayana-6-11-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-34.translation: Then Sharabha, after thought, spoke meaningful words: "Let a spy be set on him quickly, tiger among men."
ramayana-6-11-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-35.translation: "After placing a subtle-minded spy and testing him properly, then he should be accepted as is right."
ramayana-6-11-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-36.translation: Then Jambavan, wise with the insight of the scriptures, looked on and offered words full of merit and free of fault.
ramayana-6-11-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-37.translation: "Vibhishana has come from the wicked rakshasa lord, who is bound in enmity with us, at the wrong place and time. He should be suspected in every way."
ramayana-6-11-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-38.translation: Then Mainda, who knew good and bad policy, gave his more reasoned words.
ramayana-6-11-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-39.translation: "This Vibhishana is called Ravana's brother. Let him be questioned gently and slowly, lord of men."
ramayana-6-11-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-40.translation: "Knowing his intent, you will then act on the truth, whether he is found to be wicked or not, after careful thought, bull among men."
ramayana-6-11-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-41.translation: Then Hanuman, best of ministers, refined in speech, spoke gentle words, meaningful, sweet and brief.
ramayana-6-11-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-42.translation: "Not even Brihaspati speaking could outdo you, best of minds, able, best of speakers."
ramayana-6-11-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-43.translation: "I will speak, king, not from argument, nor rivalry, nor pride, nor desire, but truly, out of respect for Rama."
ramayana-6-11-43.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-44.translation: "In what your ministers said about good and harm, I see a flaw: the action they propose does not work."
ramayana-6-11-44.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-45.translation: "Without giving him a task, his ability cannot be known; yet to appoint him hastily seems a mistake to me."
ramayana-6-11-45.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-46.translation: "As for setting a spy, as your ministers advised, there is no reason for it, since it is not practical."
ramayana-6-11-46.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-47.translation: "As for 'he came at the wrong place and time', I have something to say on that; hear it as I see it."
ramayana-6-11-47.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-48.translation: "This is the very right place and time, as it happens; going from one man to another, he has seen faults and merits too."
ramayana-6-11-48.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-49.translation: "Seeing Ravana's wickedness and your valour, his coming is fitting and in keeping with his wisdom."
ramayana-6-11-49.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-50.translation: "As for 'let him be questioned by men in disguise', I have a view on that, carefully considered."
ramayana-6-11-50.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-51.translation: "Being questioned, a wise man would suddenly grow suspicious, and a friend who came in good faith, questioned falsely, would be turned against us."
ramayana-6-11-51.meaning: Suspicion can make an enemy of a friend.
ramayana-6-11-51.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-52.translation: "It is impossible, king, to know another's mind quickly. Yet I see great skill in the inner nature shown by his words."
ramayana-6-11-52.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-53.translation: "No wickedness is ever seen in him as he speaks, and his face is clear. So I have no doubt."
ramayana-6-11-53.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-54.translation: "A deceitful man does not come forward with an unsuspecting mind, at ease; and his speech is not wicked. So there is no doubt here."
ramayana-6-11-54.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-55.translation: "One's expression, though hidden, cannot be concealed; it forcibly reveals the inner feeling of men."
ramayana-6-11-55.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-56.translation: "An act suited to time and place, best of doers, done with skill, quickly bears fruit."
ramayana-6-11-56.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-57.translation: "Seeing your effort, Ravana's false conduct, hearing of Vali's death and Sugriva's crowning,"
ramayana-6-11-57.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-58.translation: "and seeking the kingdom, he has come here deliberately. With this in mind, accepting him is right."
ramayana-6-11-58.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-11-59.translation: "I have spoken as best I can about the rakshasa's honesty. Having heard, you, wisest of the wise, decide the rest."
ramayana-6-11-59.meaning: He leaves the decision to Rama.
ramayana-6-11-59.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 11: Rama's counsellors give their views on Vibhishana; Hanuman argues he is sincere.

ramayana-6-12-1.translation: Then Rama, glad at heart, having heard the son of the Wind, invincible and learned, spoke what was in his mind.
ramayana-6-12-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-2.translation: "I too have something to say about Vibhishana. I want you all, who wish me well, to hear it."
ramayana-6-12-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-3.translation: "I will never turn away one who comes in friendship. Even if he has faults, the good do not blame this."
ramayana-6-12-3.meaning: Rama's principle: never reject one who comes as a friend.
ramayana-6-12-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-4.translation: Hearing Rama's words, Sugriva, lord of monkeys, moved by friendship, replied to Kakutstha.
ramayana-6-12-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-5.translation: "What wonder is it, knower of dharma, crest-jewel of world-lords, that you speak nobly, courageous and on the good path?"
ramayana-6-12-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-6.translation: "My inner self also knows Vibhishana's purity; he has been tested in every way by inference and by his manner."
ramayana-6-12-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-7.translation: "So let wise Vibhishana quickly be equal to us, Raghava, and become our friend."
ramayana-6-12-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-8.translation: Hearing Sugriva's words and reflecting, Rama spoke even more noble words to the bull among monkeys.
ramayana-6-12-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-9.translation: "Whether this night-walker is wicked or not, he cannot do me even the slightest harm in any way."
ramayana-6-12-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-10.translation: "If I wished, lord of the monkey hosts, I could slay pishachas, danavas, yakshas and rakshasas on earth with a fingertip."
ramayana-6-12-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-11.translation: "It is told that a dove received an enemy who came for refuge, honoured him properly, and invited him to eat its own flesh."
ramayana-6-12-11.meaning: The story of the dove who sheltered its enemy.
ramayana-6-12-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-12.translation: "That dove welcomed the one who had taken away his own mate, best of monkeys; how much more should someone like me?"
ramayana-6-12-12.meaning: If a bird can shelter its enemy, how much more a king.
ramayana-6-12-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-13.translation: "Hear a righteous verse sung long ago by the great sage Kandu, truthful son of the sage Kanva."
ramayana-6-12-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-14.translation: "'One should not kill even an enemy who comes for refuge, wretched, with joined palms, begging, for the sake of kindness, scorcher of foes.'"
ramayana-6-12-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-15.translation: "'Whether in distress or proud, an enemy who has come to others for refuge must be protected by the self-disciplined even at the cost of their own lives.'"
ramayana-6-12-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-16.translation: "'If one does not protect him with all one's strength, out of fear, confusion or desire, that is a sin condemned by the world.'"
ramayana-6-12-16.meaning: Failing to protect is a great wrong.
ramayana-6-12-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-17.translation: "'If one seeking refuge perishes unprotected before his protector's eyes, he goes off taking all that protector's merit.'"
ramayana-6-12-17.meaning: The cost of failing a refugee.
ramayana-6-12-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-18.translation: "So there is great fault in not protecting those who surrender: it bars heaven, destroys fame, and ruins strength and valour."
ramayana-6-12-18.meaning: The fault of abandoning the helpless.
ramayana-6-12-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-19.translation: "I will follow Kandu's excellent words truly; they are righteous, bring fame, and lead to heaven when they bear fruit."
ramayana-6-12-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-20.translation: "To anyone who comes to me even once and asks, saying 'I am yours', I give safety from all beings. This is my vow."
ramayana-6-12-20.meaning: Rama's famous vow of refuge: whoever turns to him even once is protected. One of the most cherished verses of the Ramayana.
ramayana-6-12-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-21.translation: "Bring him, best of monkeys; I have granted him safety, whether he is Vibhishana or Ravana himself, Sugriva."
ramayana-6-12-21.meaning: Even Ravana would be protected if he surrendered.
ramayana-6-12-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-12-22.translation: Hearing Sugriva agree to what the monkey lord had been told, the lord of men quickly met Vibhishana, as Indra met the king of birds.
ramayana-6-12-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama declares that he will never turn away one who seeks refuge, and accepts Vibhishana.

ramayana-6-13-1.translation: When Raghava had granted safety, Ravana's younger brother, humble and glad, came down from the sky to the earth with his loyal followers.
ramayana-6-13-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-2.translation: Righteous Vibhishana, seeking refuge, fell at Rama's feet with the four rakshasas.
ramayana-6-13-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-3.translation: Then Vibhishana spoke to Rama words that were righteous, fitting and timely, bringing joy.
ramayana-6-13-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-4.translation: "I am Ravana's younger brother, and he insulted me. I have come for refuge to you, refuge of all beings."
ramayana-6-13-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-5.translation: "I have left Lanka, my friends and my wealth. My kingdom, my life and my happiness are now in your hands."
ramayana-6-13-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-6.translation: "I will help as much as I can in slaying the rakshasas and storming Lanka, and I will enter the army."
ramayana-6-13-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-7.translation: As he spoke, Rama embraced Vibhishana and, pleased, said to Lakshmana: "Bring water from the ocean."
ramayana-6-13-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-8.translation: "With it, honourable one, anoint this very wise Vibhishana at once as king of the rakshasas, since I am pleased."
ramayana-6-13-8.meaning: Rama crowns him even before the war.
ramayana-6-13-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-9.translation: Told this, Sumitra's son anointed Vibhishana king among the chief monkeys at Rama's command.
ramayana-6-13-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-10.translation: Seeing Rama's grace, the monkeys at once shouted loudly and said, "Well done, well done!"
ramayana-6-13-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-11.translation: Hanuman and Sugriva said to Vibhishana: "How shall we cross the unshakeable ocean, home of Varuna?"
ramayana-6-13-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-12.translation: "By what means can we approach the lord of rivers so that all of us with the army can quickly cross the ocean?"
ramayana-6-13-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-13.translation: Asked thus, Vibhishana, knower of dharma, replied: "King Raghava should go to the Ocean for help."
ramayana-6-13-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-14.translation: "This boundless great ocean was dug by Sagara. The great ocean should help Rama, a kinsman of Sagara."
ramayana-6-13-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-15.translation: When the wise rakshasa Vibhishana said this, it pleased Raghava, righteous by nature.
ramayana-6-13-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-16.translation: Radiant Rama, skilled in action, smiling, spoke to Lakshmana and Sugriva, lord of monkeys, to honour them.
ramayana-6-13-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-17.translation: "I like this advice of Vibhishana's, Lakshmana. Tell me, with Sugriva, if you like it too."
ramayana-6-13-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-18.translation: "Sugriva is always wise, and you are skilled in counsel. Having both considered it, say what seems best to you."
ramayana-6-13-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-19.translation: Told thus, the two heroes, Sugriva and Lakshmana, spoke these courteous words.
ramayana-6-13-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-20.translation: "Why would it not please us, tiger among men, Raghava? What Vibhishana says will bring good at this time."
ramayana-6-13-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-21.translation: "Without building a bridge over this terrible ocean, Lanka cannot be reached, even by gods and demons with Indra."
ramayana-6-13-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-22.translation: "Let brave Vibhishana's words be followed properly. Enough delay; let the Ocean be asked."
ramayana-6-13-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-13-23.translation: Told thus, Rama lay down on the shore of the lord of rivers, spread with kusha grass, like fire on an altar.
ramayana-6-13-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 13: Rama embraces Vibhishana and crowns him king of the rakshasas; Vibhishana advises asking the Ocean for help.

ramayana-6-14-1.translation: As Rama lay on the ground spread with kusha grass, watchful in his vow, three nights passed.
ramayana-6-14-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-2.translation: But the slow Ocean did not show himself to Rama, though Rama, pure in mind, honoured him properly.
ramayana-6-14-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-3.translation: Then Rama, angry with the Ocean, his eyes reddened at the corners, said to Lakshmana of fine marks, beside him:
ramayana-6-14-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-4.translation: "See the arrogance of the ignoble Ocean, Lakshmana, who, though honoured, does not show himself."
ramayana-6-14-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-5.translation: "Calm, patience, straightforwardness and kind speech, the virtues of the good, are taken as weakness by those without virtue."
ramayana-6-14-5.meaning: The unworthy mistake gentleness for weakness.
ramayana-6-14-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-6.translation: "The world honours the boastful, wicked, bold, aggressive man who uses force everywhere."
ramayana-6-14-6.meaning: A bitter observation about the world.
ramayana-6-14-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-7.translation: "Not by gentleness can fame be won, nor glory, Lakshmana, in this world, nor victory at the head of battle."
ramayana-6-14-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-8.translation: "Today, son of Sumitra, see the home of sea monsters, its waters blocked on all sides by floating monsters pierced by my arrows."
ramayana-6-14-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-9.translation: "See here the great coils of fish, the trunks of sea elephants, and the hoods of serpents cut apart by me, Lakshmana."
ramayana-6-14-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-10.translation: "Today with a great fight I will dry up the ocean with my arrows, with its conches, shells, fish and sea monsters."
ramayana-6-14-10.meaning: He threatens to dry the sea.
ramayana-6-14-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-11.translation: "Because I am patient, this home of sea monsters thinks me weak. Shame on patience towards such a one!"
ramayana-6-14-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-12.translation: "Bring my bow, son of Sumitra, and arrows like poisonous snakes. Today, in anger, I will shake even the unshakeable ocean."
ramayana-6-14-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-13.translation: "The ocean, which keeps its bounds at the shore though crowded with a thousand waves, I will make boundless with my arrows."
ramayana-6-14-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-14.translation: Having said this, bow in hand, eyes wide with anger, Rama became invincible, blazing like the fire at the end of an age.
ramayana-6-14-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

keywords.meaning: fire at the end of an age

ramayana-6-14-15.translation: Drawing his terrible bow and shaking the world with his arrows, he loosed fierce shafts like Indra's thunderbolts.
ramayana-6-14-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-16.translation: Those blazing, swift, excellent arrows entered the ocean's waters, terrifying the serpents.
ramayana-6-14-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-17.translation: Then a great, terrible surge arose in the ocean with its crocodiles and sea monsters, and the roar of the wind.
ramayana-6-14-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-18.translation: Suddenly the great ocean became spread with rows of great waves, full of conches and shells, its waves swirling with smoke.
ramayana-6-14-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-19.translation: The serpents with blazing mouths and eyes were in pain, and so were the mighty danavas who live in the underworld.
ramayana-6-14-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-20.translation: Waves of the king of rivers, like the Vindhya and Mandara mountains, rose up by the thousands with crocodiles and sea monsters.
ramayana-6-14-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-14-21.translation: The ocean, its masses of waves whirling, its serpents and rakshasas panicking, its great crocodiles thrown up, was churned.
ramayana-6-14-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 14: after three days of waiting, Rama loses patience with the Ocean and shoots fiery arrows into it.

ramayana-6-15-1.translation: Then from the middle of the ocean the Ocean himself rose, like the sun rising from the great mountain Meru; the Ocean appeared with serpents with blazing mouths.
ramayana-6-15-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god rises and advises Rama to build a bridge.

ramayana-6-15-2.translation: Gleaming like glossy cat's-eye, adorned with gold, wearing red garlands and garments, with eyes like lotus petals,
ramayana-6-15-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god rises and advises Rama to build a bridge.

ramayana-6-15-3.translation: the mighty Ocean came forward, greeted Rama first, and with joined palms spoke to Raghava, who held arrows in his hand.
ramayana-6-15-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god rises and advises Rama to build a bridge.

ramayana-6-15-4.translation: "Earth, wind, sky, water and fire, Raghava, stay in their own nature, gentle one, following their eternal path."
ramayana-6-15-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-5.translation: "So my nature is this: that I am deep and cannot be crossed by swimming. Any change would be against nature. I tell you this."
ramayana-6-15-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-6.translation: "Not out of desire, greed or fear, prince, could I ever still my waters full of crocodiles and sharks."
ramayana-6-15-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-7.translation: "I will arrange something, Rama, and I will bear it: the sea creatures will not attack while the army crosses."
ramayana-6-15-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-8.translation: "This, gentle one, is Nala, son of Vishvakarma, splendid, given a boon by his father, equal to Vishvakarma."
ramayana-6-15-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-9.translation: "Let this monkey of great energy build a bridge on me. I will hold it up, for he is like his father."
ramayana-6-15-9.meaning: The ocean will support the bridge.
ramayana-6-15-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-10.translation: Having said this, the Ocean vanished. Then Nala, mighty best of monkeys, rose and spoke to Rama.
ramayana-6-15-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-11.translation: "I will build a bridge across the wide ocean, relying on my father's skill. The great ocean has spoken the truth."
ramayana-6-15-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-12.translation: "Vishvakarma gave a boon to my mother on Mandara; I am his own son, equal to Vishvakarma."
ramayana-6-15-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-13.translation: "I would not speak of my own merits unless asked. Let the bulls among monkeys begin building the bridge this very day."
ramayana-6-15-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-14.translation: Then, sent out by Rama, the monkey leaders rushed joyfully into the great forest from all sides, by the hundreds of thousands.
ramayana-6-15-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-15.translation: Those mountain-like bulls among monkeys broke down trees there and dragged them to the sea.
ramayana-6-15-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-16.translation: With sala, ashvakarna, dhava, bamboo, kutaja, arjuna, palm, tilaka and timisha trees,
ramayana-6-15-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-17.translation: with bilva, saptaparna, flowering karnikara, mango and ashoka trees, the monkeys filled the sea.
ramayana-6-15-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-18.translation: The best of monkeys lifted trees, with roots and without, like Indra's banners, and carried them.
ramayana-6-15-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-19.translation: As rocks were thrown in, the water was suddenly churned up, rose into the sky, and flowed back here and there.
ramayana-6-15-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-20.translation: Nala built a great bridge, ten leagues wide and a hundred leagues long, across the middle of the lord of rivers.
ramayana-6-15-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-21.translation: As rocks were thrown and mountains dropped, a tumultuous sound arose in that great ocean.
ramayana-6-15-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-22.translation: That lovely, splendid bridge built by Nala in the sea shone like the path of Svati in the sky.
ramayana-6-15-22.meaning: The bridge like the Milky Way.
ramayana-6-15-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-23.translation: Then the gods with gandharvas, siddhas and great sages came to see.
ramayana-6-15-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-24.translation: Leaping, bounding and roaring were the monkeys; all beings saw that unimaginable, unbearable, wonderful, hair-raising bridge-building in the sea.
ramayana-6-15-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-25.translation: Those thousands of millions of mighty monkeys, building the bridge in the sea, reached the far shore of the great ocean.
ramayana-6-15-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-26.translation: Wide, well made, splendid, with good footing and firmly set, the great bridge shone like the parting line in the hair of the sea.
ramayana-6-15-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-27.translation: Then Vibhishana, mace in hand, stood on the far side of the sea with his ministers to strike any enemies.
ramayana-6-15-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-28.translation: At the head of the army went splendid Rama with Lakshmana, bow in hand, righteous, with Sugriva.
ramayana-6-15-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-29.translation: Some monkeys went down the middle, some at the sides; some fell into the water, some found no room; some leapt through the sky like Garuda.
ramayana-6-15-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-30.translation: The fearsome monkey army, crossing with a great roar, drowned out the fearsome roar of the ocean.
ramayana-6-15-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-31.translation: The monkey army crossed by Nala's bridge and camped with the king on the shore, rich in roots, fruits and water.
ramayana-6-15-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-32.translation: Seeing Raghava's wonderful, difficult deed, the gods with siddhas and charanas, together with the great sages, came to Rama and anointed him with holy water.
ramayana-6-15-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-15-33.translation: "Conquer your enemies, lord of men; rule the earth and its oceans for endless years." So they honoured Rama with many auspicious words.
ramayana-6-15-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 15: the Ocean god advises a bridge; Nala builds it, and the army crosses to Lanka.

ramayana-6-16-1.translation: When Rama, son of Dasharatha, had crossed the sea with his army, splendid Ravana spoke to his ministers Shuka and Sarana.
ramayana-6-16-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-2.translation: "The whole monkey army has crossed the impassable sea. Rama's bridge over the ocean has never been done before."
ramayana-6-16-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-3.translation: "I could never have believed a bridge over the sea. I must count that monkey army."
ramayana-6-16-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-4.translation: "Enter the monkey army unseen, and learn its size, its strength, and who are the chief monkeys,"
ramayana-6-16-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-5.translation: "who are Rama's and Sugriva's trusted ministers, who go in front, and which monkeys are brave,"
ramayana-6-16-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-6.translation: "how the bridge was built over the ocean, and how those great monkeys are camped."
ramayana-6-16-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-7.translation: "You should learn truly Rama's resolve, his strength and weapons, and heroic Lakshmana's."
ramayana-6-16-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-8.translation: "And who is the commander of those mighty monkeys. Learn this truly and come back quickly."
ramayana-6-16-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-9.translation: So ordered, the rakshasa heroes Shuka and Sarana took the form of monkeys and entered the monkey army.
ramayana-6-16-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-10.translation: But Shuka and Sarana could not count that unimaginable, hair-raising monkey army.
ramayana-6-16-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-11.translation: It filled mountain peaks, valleys and caves, the shores of the sea, forests and groves,
ramayana-6-16-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-12.translation: crossing, crossed and about to cross on every side, camped and camping, roaring fearsomely, mighty.
ramayana-6-16-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-13.translation: Radiant Vibhishana saw the two in disguise, seized Shuka and Sarana, and told Rama: "Two spies from Lanka have come, conquerors of enemy cities."
ramayana-6-16-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-14.translation: Seeing Rama, the two were shaken and hopeless of life; frightened, with joined palms, they said:
ramayana-6-16-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-15.translation: "Gentle one, we both came here sent by Ravana to learn about your whole army, joy of the Raghus."
ramayana-6-16-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-16.translation: Hearing their words, Rama, son of Dasharatha, devoted to the good of all beings, laughed and said:
ramayana-6-16-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-17.translation: "If you have seen the whole army and observed us well, or done your task as told, go back as you please."
ramayana-6-16-17.meaning: Rama lets them go. A sign of his confidence and mercy.
ramayana-6-16-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-18.translation: "Entering the city of Lanka, tell the king of rakshasas, Kubera's younger brother, my words exactly."
ramayana-6-16-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-19.translation: "'Show, as you please, with your army and kin, the strength relying on which you carried off my Sita.'"
ramayana-6-16-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-20.translation: "'Tomorrow you will see the city of Lanka with its walls and gates, and the rakshasa army, destroyed by my arrows.'"
ramayana-6-16-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-21.translation: "'I will let loose terrible anger, Ravana; hold on to your strength. Tomorrow I will be like Indra hurling his thunderbolt on the danavas.'"
ramayana-6-16-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-22.translation: So instructed, the rakshasas Shuka and Sarana came to the city of Lanka and spoke to the rakshasa lord.
ramayana-6-16-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-23.translation: "Lord of rakshasas, we were seized by Vibhishana and deserved death, but righteous Rama of boundless power saw us and set us free."
ramayana-6-16-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-24.translation: "Where four bulls among men stand together, heroes like the world-guardians, skilled in weapons, firm in valour,"
ramayana-6-16-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-25.translation: "Rama son of Dasharatha, splendid Lakshmana, Vibhishana, and radiant Sugriva, valiant as great Indra,"
ramayana-6-16-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-26.translation: "these alone could uproot the city of Lanka with its walls and gates and move it elsewhere; let all the monkeys stand aside."
ramayana-6-16-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-27.translation: "Such is Rama's form and weapons that he alone will destroy the city of Lanka; let the other three stand aside."
ramayana-6-16-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-28.translation: "That army, guarded by Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva, has become harder to defeat than by all the gods and demons together."
ramayana-6-16-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-16-29.translation: "The army of the great forest-dwellers is joyful and eager to fight now. Enough of conflict; let peace be made. Let Maithili be given to Dasharatha's son."
ramayana-6-16-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 16: Ravana sends the spies Shuka and Sarana; they are caught, and Rama lets them go with a message.

ramayana-6-17-1.translation: Hearing the beneficial and bold words spoken by Sarana, King Ravana replied to Sarana.
ramayana-6-17-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-2.translation: "Even if gods, gandharvas and danavas attacked me, I would not give up Sita, even for fear of all the worlds."
ramayana-6-17-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-3.translation: "You, gentle one, are frightened, badly beaten by the monkeys, and so you think it right to return Sita today. What enemy could defeat me in battle?"
ramayana-6-17-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-4.translation: Having spoken these harsh words, splendid Ravana, lord of rakshasas, climbed his snow-white palace, many palm-trees high, wishing to see.
ramayana-6-17-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-5.translation: With the two spies, Ravana, beside himself with rage, looking at the sea, mountains and forests, saw the land filled with monkeys.
ramayana-6-17-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-6.translation: Seeing that boundless, countless great monkey army, King Ravana asked Sarana:
ramayana-6-17-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-7.translation: "Among these monkey chiefs, who are brave, who are mighty? Who go in front with great energy on all sides?"
ramayana-6-17-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-8.translation: "To whom does Sugriva listen? Who are the leaders of leaders? Sarana, tell me everything: who are the chief monkeys?"
ramayana-6-17-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-9.translation: Sarana, who knew the chiefs, pointed out the chief forest-dwellers to the questioning rakshasa lord.
ramayana-6-17-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-10.translation: "That monkey standing facing Lanka, roaring, surrounded by a hundred thousand leaders,"
ramayana-6-17-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-11.translation: "at whose great roar all Lanka trembles with its walls, gates, mountains and forests,"
ramayana-6-17-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-12.translation: "standing at the head of the army of great Sugriva, lord of all monkeys, is the hero leader named Nila."
ramayana-6-17-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-13.translation: "The mighty one who walks the earth on his feet holding his arms, who faces Lanka in anger and yawns again and again,"
ramayana-6-17-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-14.translation: "like a mountain peak, the colour of lotus filaments, who in rage lashes his tail again and again,"
ramayana-6-17-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-15.translation: "at the sound of whose tail the ten directions seem to echo: this is Angada, crowned crown prince by Sugriva, king of monkeys, and he challenges you to battle."
ramayana-6-17-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-16.translation: "Those bulls among monkeys who stretch their limbs, shriek and roar, and rise and yawn in anger,"
ramayana-6-17-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-17.translation: "these are fearsome, unbearable, fierce and fiercely valiant: eight hundred thousand and a thousand million."
ramayana-6-17-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-18.translation: "The heroes from the sandal forests who follow him; he hopes to crush Lanka with his own troops."
ramayana-6-17-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-19.translation: "Shveta, silver-coloured, strong, fearsome in valour, wise, brave, famous in the three worlds."
ramayana-6-17-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-20.translation: "That monkey goes quickly to Sugriva and back again, dividing the monkey army and cheering the troops."
ramayana-6-17-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-21.translation: "He who once roamed the lovely mountain on the bank of the Gomati, named Sankochana, full of many trees,"
ramayana-6-17-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-22.translation: "rules there: the leader named Kumuda, who leads a hundred thousand thousand."
ramayana-6-17-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-23.translation: "Whose hair, many arm-spans long, red, yellow, grey and white, hangs from his long tail, of fearsome deeds,"
ramayana-6-17-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-24.translation: "undaunted, wrathful, fierce, he longs for battle; he too hopes to crush Lanka with his own troops."
ramayana-6-17-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-25.translation: "That tawny one like a lion, with a long mane, watching Lanka steadily as if to burn it with his eyes,"
ramayana-6-17-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-26.translation: "who always lives on the Vindhya, the Krishna mountain, Sahya and Sudarshana, king, is the leader named Rambha."
ramayana-6-17-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-27.translation: "A hundred and thirty hundred thousand monkey leaders surround and follow him to crush Lanka with might."
ramayana-6-17-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-28.translation: "He who spreads his ears and yawns again and again, who does not fear death nor run from the troop,"
ramayana-6-17-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-29.translation: "mighty and fearless, who always lives on lovely Mount Salveya, king, is the leader named Sharabha."
ramayana-6-17-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-30.translation: "All his mighty leaders are called Viharas, king: a hundred and forty thousand of them."
ramayana-6-17-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-31.translation: "He who stands covering the sky like a great cloud, among the monkey heroes like Indra among the gods,"
ramayana-6-17-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-32.translation: "whose great roar like drums is heard among the monkey lords longing for battle,"
ramayana-6-17-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-33.translation: "who lives on the matchless Pariyatra mountain, always unbearable in battle, is the leader named Panasa."
ramayana-6-17-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-34.translation: "Fifty hundred thousand leaders serve him, best of leaders, each with their troops in divisions."
ramayana-6-17-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-35.translation: "He who stands adorning the fearsome, leaping army on the sea shore like a second ocean,"
ramayana-6-17-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-36.translation: "like Mount Dardara, is the leader named Vinata, who wanders drinking from the Parnasha, best of rivers."
ramayana-6-17-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-37.translation: "His force is sixty hundred thousand monkeys. The leader named Krathana challenges you to battle."
ramayana-6-17-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-38.translation: "The monkey whose body has the colour of red ochre, radiant Gavaya, comes at you in anger."
ramayana-6-17-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-39.translation: "Seventy hundred thousand serve him; he hopes to crush Lanka with his own troops."
ramayana-6-17-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-17-40.translation: "These unbearable, fearsome, mighty leaders, best of leaders, who can take any form, are beyond counting."
ramayana-6-17-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana refuses to return Sita and climbs a tower; Sarana points out the monkey leaders.

ramayana-6-18-1.translation: "I will tell you about those leaders as you watch, who show valour for Raghava's sake and do not guard their lives."
ramayana-6-18-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-2.translation: "His long, glossy hair, dark, copper, yellow and white, hangs spread from his tail; he is fierce in deeds."
ramayana-6-18-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-3.translation: "When it is raised it shines like the rays of the sun, and it trails along the ground. This leader is named Hara."
ramayana-6-18-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-4.translation: "Behind him follow hundreds and thousands, holding up trees together, eager to climb onto Lanka."
ramayana-6-18-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-5.translation: "With a thousand crores of mighty monkeys, conqueror of enemy cities, he hopes to beat you in battle."
ramayana-6-18-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-6.translation: "Those you see standing like great dark clouds, black, true in valour in battle..."
ramayana-6-18-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-7.translation: "...heroes whose weapons are claws and teeth, sharp in anger and fearsome, countless, beyond naming, like the far shore of the ocean..."
ramayana-6-18-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-8.translation: "...these fierce bears, king, who live in the mountains, rough lands and rivers, are coming against you."
ramayana-6-18-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-9.translation: "In their midst, king, stands one with terrible eyes and a terrible look, surrounded on all sides like the rain god by clouds."
ramayana-6-18-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-10.translation: "He lives on Rikshavan, best of mountains, drinking the Narmada's water. He is lord of all the bears, the leader named Dhumra."
ramayana-6-18-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-11.translation: "Look at his younger brother, like a mountain, alike in form to his brother but greater in valour."
ramayana-6-18-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-12.translation: "This is Jambavan, leader of great leaders: calm, obedient to his elders, yet fierce in battle."
ramayana-6-18-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-13.translation: "This wise Jambavan gave great help to Indra in the war of gods and demons, and won many boons."
ramayana-6-18-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-14.translation: "Climbing mountain peaks, these huge ones hurl rocks as big as great clouds, and they do not fear death."
ramayana-6-18-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-15.translation: "Many in his army roam about, hairy like goblins and demons, bright as fire."
ramayana-6-18-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-16.translation: "The one all the monkeys watch, standing excited as if about to leap, a leader of leaders..."
ramayana-6-18-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-17.translation: "...he, king, once served thousand-eyed Indra. Strong in might, this leader is named Rambha."
ramayana-6-18-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-18.translation: "The one who, walking, brushes with his side a mountain a yojana away, and whose body reaches a yojana high..."
ramayana-6-18-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-19.translation: "...than whom there is no finer form among four-footed beings, he is known as Sannadana, grandfather of the monkeys."
ramayana-6-18-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-20.translation: "He once gave battle to wise Indra and was not defeated. He is a leader of leaders, whose valour when he strides out is like Indra's."
ramayana-6-18-20.meaning: He held his own against Indra.
ramayana-6-18-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-21.translation: "He was born to a gandharva maiden from the Fire god, long ago in the war of gods and demons, to help the gods."
ramayana-6-18-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-22.translation: "Where King Vaishravana enjoys the rose-apple tree, on the king of mountains served by many kinnaras..."
ramayana-6-18-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-23.translation: "...the place that always gives pleasure to your brother, lord of demons. There lives this glorious, strong bull of monkeys, never boastful in battle, the leader named Krathana."
ramayana-6-18-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana. Not boasting is praised as a mark of a true hero.

ramayana-6-18-24.translation: "Surrounded by a thousand crores of monkeys, he hopes to crush Lanka with his own troop."
ramayana-6-18-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-25.translation: "The one who roams along the Ganga frightening elephant leaders, remembering the old enmity between elephants and monkeys..."
ramayana-6-18-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-26.translation: "...this leader and guide, who lives in mountain caves, chief of the monkey army, moving along the river from the Himalaya..."
ramayana-6-18-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-27.translation: "...who, keeping to Mount Ushirabija like Mandara, enjoys himself there as Indra does in heaven..."
ramayana-6-18-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-28.translation: "...a thousand hundred-thousands follow him. He is hard to withstand, king, the leader named Pramathi."
ramayana-6-18-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-29.translation: "The one you see like a cloud tossed by the wind, turning about many times, where all that dust rises..."
ramayana-6-18-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-30.translation: "...these fierce, black-faced, mighty golangula monkeys, a hundred hundred-thousands, who saw the bridge being built..."
ramayana-6-18-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-31.translation: "...surround the swift golangula leader named Gavaksha and advance to crush Lanka with force."
ramayana-6-18-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-32.translation: "Where bees roam and trees give every desired fruit, the mountain that the sun goes around, coloured like the sun..."
ramayana-6-18-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-33.translation: "...by whose light the beasts and birds always shine with its colour, whose slopes great sages never leave..."
ramayana-6-18-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-34.translation: "...there, king, on the lovely golden mountain, lives this leader, chief of monkey chiefs, named Kesari."
ramayana-6-18-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-35.translation: "There are sixty thousand lovely golden mountains, and in their midst is the best mountain, as you are among demons, sinless one."
ramayana-6-18-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-36.translation: "There, on that best mountain, live tawny, white, copper-faced, honey-coloured ones, armed with sharp teeth and claws."
ramayana-6-18-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-37.translation: "Four-fanged like lions, hard to approach like tigers, all equal to fire, like blazing venomous snakes."
ramayana-6-18-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-38.translation: "With long curled tails, like elephants in rut, like great mountains, roaring like great clouds."
ramayana-6-18-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-39.translation: "Their mighty lord stands in their midst, famed on earth, king, by the name Shatabali. He hopes to crush Lanka with his own troop."
ramayana-6-18-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-40.translation: "Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Nala and the monkey Nila: each is surrounded by ten crores of troops."
ramayana-6-18-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-41.translation: "And other best of monkeys who live on the Vindhya mountains, quick in stride, cannot be counted, they are so many."
ramayana-6-18-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-18-42.translation: "All of them, great king, have great power; all have bodies like great mountains; all could in a moment turn the earth into scattered, shattered hills."
ramayana-6-18-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 18: Sarana continues naming the monkey leaders for Ravana.

ramayana-6-19-1.translation: Hearing Sarana's words, Shuka, looking over the whole army, then spoke to Ravana, lord of demons.
ramayana-6-19-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-2.translation: "Those you see standing like rutting great elephants, like banyans by the Ganga or sal trees of the Himalaya..."
ramayana-6-19-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-3.translation: "...they are hard to face, king, strong, able to change form at will, like daityas and danavas, with the valour of gods in battle."
ramayana-6-19-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-4.translation: "Their number is thousands of crores, nine, five and seven, and as many shankhas and hundreds of vrindas."
ramayana-6-19-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-5.translation: "These are Sugriva's counsellors, who always live in Kishkindha, monkeys born of gods and gandharvas, changing form at will."
ramayana-6-19-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-6.translation: "Those two young ones you see standing, godlike in form, are Mainda and Dvivida; no one equals them in battle."
ramayana-6-19-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-7.translation: "With Brahma's permission both drank the nectar of immortality. They hope to crush Lanka with force in battle."
ramayana-6-19-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-8.translation: "Those two standing beside them like mountains are Sumukha and Vimukha, sons of Death, equal to their father."
ramayana-6-19-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-9.translation: "The one you see standing like a rutting elephant, the monkey who in anger could churn up even the ocean by his strength..."
ramayana-6-19-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-10.translation: "...he is the one who came to Lanka, to Vaidehi and to you, lord. See this monkey you saw before, come again."
ramayana-6-19-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-11.translation: "Eldest son of Kesari, known as son of the Wind, famed as Hanuman, by whom the ocean was leapt."
ramayana-6-19-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-12.translation: "Best of monkeys, changing form at will, full of strength and beauty, his course cannot be stopped, like the ever-moving Wind himself."
ramayana-6-19-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-13.translation: "As a child, they say, seeing the sun rising, and being hungry, he leapt three thousand yojanas..."
ramayana-6-19-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva. This is the well-loved story of baby Hanuman leaping for the sun, thinking it a fruit.

ramayana-6-19-14.translation: "...thinking, 'I will grab the sun; my hunger will not go away otherwise,' proud of his strength."
ramayana-6-19-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-15.translation: "Not reaching that god, who cannot be touched even by divine sages and demons, he fell on the mountain where the sun rises."
ramayana-6-19-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-16.translation: "As this monkey fell, one jaw was slightly broken on the rocky ground. Because of that strong jaw he is called Hanuman."
ramayana-6-19-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva. 'Hanuman' is understood to mean 'one with a (marked) jaw'.

ramayana-6-19-17.translation: "Truly I know this monkey from reliable reports. His strength, form and power cannot be described."
ramayana-6-19-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-18.translation: "He alone hopes to crush Lanka with force. And the one next to him, the hero, dark, with lotus eyes..."
ramayana-6-19-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva.

ramayana-6-19-19.translation: "...the great chariot warrior of the Ikshvakus, famed in the world for valour, in whom dharma never wavers and who never goes beyond dharma..."
ramayana-6-19-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 19: Shuka names the remaining leaders, among them Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and Sugriva. Even the enemy's spy describes Rama by his unbroken dharma.

ramayana-6-19-20.translation: "...who knows the Brahma weapon and the Vedas, best of those who know the Vedas, who could split the sky with arrows and break mountains..."
