ramayana-6-27-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. These are Ravana's proud words; the story does not endorse them.

ramayana-6-27-7.translation: "What wise man who knows the truth of the scriptures would speak harshly to a powerful king on his throne, unless urged by the enemy?"
ramayana-6-27-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. These are Ravana's proud words; the story does not endorse them.

ramayana-6-27-8.translation: "Having brought Sita from the forest, like Lakshmi without her lotus, why should I give her back out of fear of Raghava?"
ramayana-6-27-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. These are Ravana's proud words; the story does not endorse them.

ramayana-6-27-9.translation: "In a few days you will see Raghava, with Sugriva and Lakshmana, surrounded by crores of monkeys, killed by me."
ramayana-6-27-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. These are Ravana's proud words; the story does not endorse them.

ramayana-6-27-10.translation: "Even gods do not stand before me in single combat. Why would Ravana feel fear in battle?"
ramayana-6-27-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. These are Ravana's proud words; the story does not endorse them.

ramayana-6-27-11.translation: "I may break in two, but I will not bow to anyone. This is my inborn flaw, a nature hard to overcome."
ramayana-6-27-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. Ravana himself names his stubbornness as a flaw. Being unable to bend is a weakness, not a strength.

ramayana-6-27-12.translation: "If Rama happened to build a bridge over the sea, what is so amazing about that, that it made you afraid?"
ramayana-6-27-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. These are Ravana's proud words; the story does not endorse them.

ramayana-6-27-13.translation: "I promise you truly: having crossed the ocean with the monkey army, Rama will not go back alive."
ramayana-6-27-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates. These are Ravana's proud words; the story does not endorse them.

ramayana-6-27-14.translation: Seeing Ravana so excited and angry as he spoke, Malyavan, ashamed, gave no answer.
ramayana-6-27-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-15.translation: Blessing the king with a wish for victory, as was proper, Malyavan took his leave and went home.
ramayana-6-27-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-16.translation: Ravana, after consulting and thinking with his ministers, had matchless defences set up in Lanka.
ramayana-6-27-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-17.translation: He posted the demon Prahasta at the eastern gate, and the mighty Mahaparshva and Mahodara at the southern.
ramayana-6-27-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-18.translation: At the western gate he posted his son Indrajit, great in magic, surrounded by many demons.
ramayana-6-27-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-19.translation: Assigning Shuka and Sarana to the northern city gate, he told the ministers, "I will be there myself."
ramayana-6-27-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-20.translation: He placed the demon Virupaksha, of great strength and valour, in the central camp with many demons.
ramayana-6-27-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-21.translation: Having made these arrangements in Lanka, the bull among demons thought his goal achieved, though he was in the power of Death.
ramayana-6-27-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-27-22.translation: Then he dismissed the ministers after ordering full arrangements for the city, and honoured by them with blessings for victory, entered his great, rich inner palace.
ramayana-6-27-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 27: Ravana angrily rejects Malyavan's advice and posts guards at Lanka's gates.

ramayana-6-28-1.translation: The kings of men and monkeys, the monkey son of the Wind, Jambavan king of bears, and the demon Vibhishana...
ramayana-6-28-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-2.translation: ...Angada son of Vali, Saumitri, the monkey Sharabha, Sushena with his kin, Mainda and Dvivida...
ramayana-6-28-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-3.translation: ...Gaja, Gavaksha, Kumuda, Nala and Panasa, having reached the enemy's land, met and took counsel.
ramayana-6-28-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-4.translation: "There is Lanka, the city guarded by Ravana, hard to conquer even by asuras, serpents, gandharvas and gods."
ramayana-6-28-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-5.translation: "Keep success in mind and plan to decide this, for Ravana, lord of demons, is always present here."
ramayana-6-28-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-6.translation: As they spoke, Ravana's younger brother Vibhishana spoke words that were refined and full of meaning.
ramayana-6-28-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-7.translation: "Anala, Sharabha, Sampati and Praghasa, my ministers, went to the city of Lanka and have come back here."
ramayana-6-28-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-8.translation: "Taking the form of birds they entered the enemy forces, saw the arrangements made, and have returned."
ramayana-6-28-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-9.translation: "Rama, hear from me all of wicked Ravana's arrangements, exactly as they told them."
ramayana-6-28-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-10.translation: "Prahasta with his force stands at the eastern gate; mighty Mahaparshva and Mahodara at the southern."
ramayana-6-28-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-11.translation: "Indrajit holds the western gate, surrounded by many demons with spears, swords and bows, holding tridents and hammers."
ramayana-6-28-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-12.translation: "Ravana's son is surrounded by heroes with many weapons, by many thousands of armed demons."
ramayana-6-28-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-13.translation: "Very anxious, surrounded by many demons, Ravana himself holds the northern city gate."
ramayana-6-28-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-14.translation: "Virupaksha with a great force armed with tridents, swords and bows holds the central camp with demons."
ramayana-6-28-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-15.translation: "Having seen these posts set up in Lanka, all my ministers came back here quickly."
ramayana-6-28-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-16.translation: "In the city there are a thousand elephants, ten thousand chariots, twenty thousand horses and more than a crore of demons."
ramayana-6-28-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-17.translation: "These night-rovers, bold, strong and violent in battle, are always dear to the demon king."
ramayana-6-28-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-18.translation: "Here, lord of men, for battle each demon has a retinue of a thousand thousands."
ramayana-6-28-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-19.translation: Having given this news of Lanka as his ministers told it, Vibhishana then said this to lotus-eyed Rama:
ramayana-6-28-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-20.translation: "When Ravana fought Kubera, Rama, sixty hundred-thousand demons marched out."
ramayana-6-28-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-21.translation: "They were like wicked Ravana in courage, strength, energy, firmness and pride."
ramayana-6-28-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-22.translation: "Do not be angry at this; I do not mean to anger or frighten you. You are able by your valour to subdue even the gods."
ramayana-6-28-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-23.translation: "So you, surrounded by a great fourfold army, arranging this monkey host, will crush Ravana."
ramayana-6-28-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-24.translation: As Ravana's younger brother said this, Raghava spoke these words to strike back at the enemy.
ramayana-6-28-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-25.translation: "At Lanka's eastern gate let Nila, bull among monkeys, fight Prahasta, surrounded by many monkeys."
ramayana-6-28-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-26.translation: "Let Angada son of Vali, with a great force, press Mahaparshva and Mahodara at the southern gate."
ramayana-6-28-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-27.translation: "Let Hanuman, son of the Wind, of boundless spirit, press the western gate and enter, surrounded by many monkeys."
ramayana-6-28-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-28.translation: "He who loves to harm hosts of daityas and danavas and great sages, the mean one, strong through boons..."
ramayana-6-28-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-29.translation: "...who roams all the worlds tormenting beings: I myself am set on killing that lord of demons."
ramayana-6-28-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-30.translation: "With Saumitri I will press the northern city gate and enter, with my force, where Ravana is."
ramayana-6-28-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-31.translation: "Let the mighty monkey king, Jambavan king of bears, and the demon king's brother be at the central post."
ramayana-6-28-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-32.translation: "The monkeys must not take human form in battle. Let this be our sign in this battle for the monkey army."
ramayana-6-28-32.meaning: A sign to tell friend from foe.
ramayana-6-28-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-33.translation: "Monkeys will be the mark among our own people. But we seven will fight the enemy in human form."
ramayana-6-28-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-34.translation: "I with my mighty brother Lakshmana, and fifth, my friend Vibhishana with his four."
ramayana-6-28-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-35.translation: Having said this to Vibhishana to achieve his goal, wise Rama decided to climb Suvela.
ramayana-6-28-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-28-36.translation: Then great Rama, covering the whole earth with his great army, happy in look, went toward Lanka, having made up his mind to kill the enemy.
ramayana-6-28-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 28: Vibhishana reports Lanka's defences and Rama assigns leaders to each gate.

ramayana-6-29-1.translation: Having decided to climb Suvela, Rama, followed by Lakshmana, said to Sugriva...
ramayana-6-29-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-2.translation: ...and to the night-rover Vibhishana, devoted, knowing dharma, counsel and rules, in gentle, noble words:
ramayana-6-29-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-3.translation: "Let us all climb this fine king of mountains, Suvela, rich with hundreds of minerals, and spend this night here."
ramayana-6-29-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-4.translation: "We will look at Lanka, home of that demon, by whom, wicked one, my wife was carried off to his own death."
ramayana-6-29-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-5.translation: "By whom dharma, good conduct and family were not understood, who did that shameful deed with base demon thinking."
ramayana-6-29-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-6.translation: "At the mention of that lowest of demons my anger grows; through the fault of that base one I will see the death of demons."
ramayana-6-29-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-7.translation: "One person, caught in the noose of Time, does wrong; and through that base one's own misdeed his whole family is destroyed."
ramayana-6-29-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka. One person's wrongdoing can bring ruin on everyone around them.

ramayana-6-29-8.translation: Talking this way, angry at Ravana, Rama climbed Suvela, with its many-coloured slopes, to stay there.
ramayana-6-29-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-9.translation: Behind him came Lakshmana, attentive, raising his great bow with arrows, eager for valour.
ramayana-6-29-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-10.translation: After him climbed Sugriva with his ministers and Vibhishana, and Hanuman, Angada, Nila, Mainda and Dvivida...
ramayana-6-29-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-11.translation: ...Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sharabha, Gandhamadana, Panasa, Kumuda, Hara and the leader Rambha.
ramayana-6-29-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-12.translation: These and many other swift monkeys, mountain-dwellers fast as the wind, climbed in hundreds onto Suvela, where Raghava was.
ramayana-6-29-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-13.translation: Quickly climbing the mountain on all sides, they saw from its peak the city, as if hanging in the sky.
ramayana-6-29-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-14.translation: The monkey leaders saw Lanka, lovely, with fine gates, adorned with fine walls, full of demons.
ramayana-6-29-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-15.translation: With dark night-rovers standing on the wall tops, the best of monkeys saw what looked like another wall.
ramayana-6-29-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-16.translation: Seeing the demons eager for battle, all the monkeys gave great roars there as Rama watched.
ramayana-6-29-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-17.translation: Then the sun set, coloured by twilight, and night came on, lit by the full moon as its lamp.
ramayana-6-29-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-29-18.translation: Then Rama, lord of the monkey army, welcomed and honoured by Vibhishana, with Lakshmana and surrounded by troops, stayed comfortably on Suvela's top.
ramayana-6-29-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 29: Rama and the army climb Mount Suvela and look at Lanka.

ramayana-6-30-1.translation: Having spent that night on Suvela, the heroic monkeys saw the forests and gardens in Lanka.
ramayana-6-30-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-2.translation: Seeing them, pleasant, lovely, wide and long, delightful to see, they were amazed.
ramayana-6-30-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-3.translation: It was full of champaka, ashoka, punnaga, sala and palm trees, covered with tamala groves, surrounded by rows of naga trees.
ramayana-6-30-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-4.translation: With hintala, arjuna, nipa, flowering saptaparna, tilaka, karnikara and patala trees all around...
ramayana-6-30-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-5.translation: ...Lanka shone with many kinds of divine trees with flowering tops wrapped in creepers, like Indra's Amaravati.
ramayana-6-30-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-6.translation: With many-coloured flowers, tender red shoots, dark green lawns and bright rows of woods...
ramayana-6-30-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-7.translation: ...the trees there bore fragrant, lovely flowers and fruits, like people wearing ornaments.
ramayana-6-30-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-8.translation: That lovely forest, like Chaitraratha and Nandana, flowering in all seasons and full of bees, shone.
ramayana-6-30-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and gardens.

ramayana-6-30-9.translation: In the forest by the waterfalls were heard the cries of gallinules and koyashtibhaka birds, dancing peacocks and cuckoos.
ramayana-6-30-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-10.translation: The groves had birds always joyful, roamed by bees, thick with cuckoos, ringing with bird calls...
ramayana-6-30-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-11.translation: ...sung in by bhringaraja birds, visited by bees, echoing with konalaka calls and the cries of cranes.
ramayana-6-30-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-12.translation: Then the heroic monkeys, changing form at will, entered those forests and gardens, glad and joyful.
ramayana-6-30-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-13.translation: As the mighty monkeys entered, a breeze blew, fragrant with flowers and pleasant to smell.
ramayana-6-30-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-14.translation: Other leaders, leaving the troops of monkey heroes with Sugriva's permission, went to Lanka, bright with banners.
ramayana-6-30-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-15.translation: Scaring birds, frightening deer and elephants, shaking Lanka with their roars, the best of roarers went on.
ramayana-6-30-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-16.translation: Swift as they were, they pressed the earth with their feet, and dust raised by their feet rose up suddenly.
ramayana-6-30-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-17.translation: Bears, lions, boars, buffaloes, elephants and deer, terrified by the noise, fled in fear in all ten directions.
ramayana-6-30-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-18.translation: Trikuta's one tall peak touching the sky, covered with flowers all around, like silver...
ramayana-6-30-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-19.translation: ...a hundred yojanas wide, clear, lovely to see, smooth, splendid and vast, hard to reach even for birds...
ramayana-6-30-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-20.translation: ...hard to climb even in thought, let alone by people in deed: on that peak sat Lanka, guarded by Ravana.
ramayana-6-30-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-21.translation: The city shone with high gate-towers like white clouds, and with golden and silver walls.
ramayana-6-30-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-22.translation: Lanka was richly adorned with palaces and mansions, like the middle sky of Vishnu with clouds at the end of summer.
ramayana-6-30-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-23.translation: There a palace adorned with a thousand pillars was seen, shaped like Kailasa's peak, as if scraping the sky.
ramayana-6-30-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-24.translation: That temple-like palace of the demon king was the city's jewel, always guarded by a full hundred demons.
ramayana-6-30-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-25.translation: Glorious Rama, Lakshmana's elder brother, whose purpose was rich, saw with the monkeys that rich city of Ravana.
ramayana-6-30-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-30-26.translation: Rama with his great army saw that city full of jewels, with many arrangements, adorned with rows of palaces, its chief gates fitted with great machines.
ramayana-6-30-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 30: from Suvela the monkeys see Lanka's lovely forests and the city on Trikuta's peak.

ramayana-6-31-1.translation: Then, seeing omens there, Lakshmana's elder brother said this to the fortunate Lakshmana:
ramayana-6-31-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-2.translation: "Taking cool water and forests full of fruit, let us divide this mass of troops and stand in formation, Lakshmana."
ramayana-6-31-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-3.translation: "I see a terrible danger at hand that will destroy the world, a slaughter of the best heroes of bears, monkeys and demons."
ramayana-6-31-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-4.translation: "Winds blow harshly, the earth shakes, mountain peaks tremble and hills fall."
ramayana-6-31-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-5.translation: "Harsh clouds like flesh-eaters, with harsh thunder, cruelly rain down rain mixed with drops of blood."
ramayana-6-31-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-6.translation: "Twilight, like red sandal, is very dreadful, and a blazing ring of fire falls from the sun."
ramayana-6-31-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-7.translation: "Unlucky beasts and birds, wretched, with wretched voices, howl toward the sun, causing great fear."
ramayana-6-31-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-8.translation: "At night the moon, without light, burns, its rays edged with black and red, as at the end of the world."
ramayana-6-31-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-9.translation: "A small, harsh, unlucky, deep red halo, and a dark mark on the sun's disc are seen, Lakshmana."
ramayana-6-31-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-10.translation: "The stars do not appear as they should. See, Lakshmana, it foretells something like the end of an age for the world."
ramayana-6-31-10.meaning: Like the end of an age.
ramayana-6-31-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-11.translation: "Crows, hawks and vultures swoop low, and jackals cry inauspicious cries loudly."
ramayana-6-31-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Omens like these show that a great battle is near.

ramayana-6-31-12.translation: "Let us quickly attack today, with speed, the unassailable city guarded by Ravana, surrounded on all sides by monkeys."
ramayana-6-31-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-13.translation: Saying this to Lakshmana, the mighty hero, Lakshmana's elder, quickly came down from the mountain top.
ramayana-6-31-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-14.translation: Coming down from that mountain, righteous Raghava looked at his own army, very hard for enemies to resist.
ramayana-6-31-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-15.translation: With Sugriva he readied the great army of the monkey king, and Raghava, who knew timing, urged it into battle at the right time.
ramayana-6-31-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-16.translation: Then at the right time the mighty-armed archer, surrounded by a great army, set out in front toward the city of Lanka.
ramayana-6-31-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-17.translation: Vibhishana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan, Nala, the king of bears, Nila and Lakshmana followed him.
ramayana-6-31-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-18.translation: Behind came the vast army of bears and forest-dwellers, covering wide ground, following Raghava.
ramayana-6-31-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-19.translation: The elephant-like monkeys, who could hold back enemies, grabbed hundreds of mountain peaks and grown trees.
ramayana-6-31-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-20.translation: In a short time the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana, tamers of foes, reached Ravana's city of Lanka.
ramayana-6-31-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-21.translation: It was garlanded with banners, lovely, adorned with parks and woods, with bright ramparts, very hard to reach, with high walls and arches.
ramayana-6-31-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-22.translation: Urged by Rama's words, the forest-dwellers pressed that city, hard to assail even for gods, and took up their posts as ordered.
ramayana-6-31-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-23.translation: Rama the archer, with his younger brother, guarded and blocked Lanka's northern gate, high as a mountain peak.
ramayana-6-31-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-24.translation: Heroic Rama, son of Dasharatha, followed by Lakshmana, camped before Lanka, the city guarded by Ravana.
ramayana-6-31-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-25.translation: He reached the northern gate where Ravana stood; no one but Rama could guard that gate.
ramayana-6-31-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-26.translation: It was held by Ravana, fearsome as the sea held by Varuna, guarded all round by fearsome armed demons, terrifying to the weak, like the underworld by danavas.
ramayana-6-31-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-27.translation: He saw many different heaps of weapons and armour laid out for the warriors.
ramayana-6-31-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-28.translation: Reaching the eastern gate, Nila, commander of the monkey army, stood with Mainda and mighty Dvivida.
ramayana-6-31-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-29.translation: Very mighty Angada took the southern gate with Rishabha, Gavaksha, Gaja and Gavaya.
ramayana-6-31-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-30.translation: Strong monkey Hanuman guarded the western gate, joined by Pramathi, Praghasa and other heroes.
ramayana-6-31-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-31.translation: Sugriva himself stood in the central post with all the best monkeys, like Garuda and the wind.
ramayana-6-31-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-32.translation: Thirty-six crores of famous monkey leaders pressed close and camped where the monkey Sugriva was.
ramayana-6-31-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-33.translation: At Rama's order Lakshmana with Vibhishana posted a crore of monkeys at each gate.
ramayana-6-31-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-34.translation: West of Rama, not far, Sugriva with Jambavan stood in the central post with many troops.
ramayana-6-31-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-35.translation: Those tigers among monkeys, toothed like tigers, holding trees and mountain tops, stood joyfully ready for battle.
ramayana-6-31-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-36.translation: All had tails twisted up, all had teeth and claws as weapons, all had bodies of strange colours, all had fierce faces.
ramayana-6-31-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-37.translation: Some had the strength of ten elephants, some ten times more, some equal in valour to a thousand elephants.
ramayana-6-31-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-38.translation: Some had the strength of whole hosts, some a hundred times more, and other monkey leaders there had boundless strength.
ramayana-6-31-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-39.translation: Their gathering was wonderful and strange, the monkey army rising like a swarm of locusts.
ramayana-6-31-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-40.translation: The sky seemed full and the earth covered by the monkeys camped round Lanka and rushing about.
ramayana-6-31-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-41.translation: A hundred hundred-thousands of bears and monkeys each came to Lanka's gates, and others to fight all around.
ramayana-6-31-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-42.translation: The mountain was surrounded on all sides by those monkeys; a thousand ten-thousands advanced on the city.
ramayana-6-31-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-43.translation: Surrounded on all sides by strong monkeys with trees in their hands, Lanka became hard to enter even for the wind.
ramayana-6-31-43.meaning: Not even the wind gets in.
ramayana-6-31-43.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-44.translation: The demons were amazed, suddenly hemmed in by monkeys like clouds, with valour like Indra's.
ramayana-6-31-44.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-45.translation: A great sound arose there from the advancing mass of troops, like the roar of water from a burst ocean.
ramayana-6-31-45.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-46.translation: With that great sound all Lanka shook, with its walls, gates, hills, woods and groves.
ramayana-6-31-46.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-47.translation: That army, guarded by Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva, became harder to assail than even all the gods and demons.
ramayana-6-31-47.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-48.translation: Having placed his army like this to destroy the demons, Raghava consulted with his counsellors and decided again and again.
ramayana-6-31-48.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-49.translation: Wishing to do things in proper order, knowing the right sequence and purpose, with Vibhishana's agreement, remembering the duty of kings, he called Angada son of Vali and said:
ramayana-6-31-49.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Even now, Rama offers a chance for peace before fighting, as a king's duty requires.

ramayana-6-31-50.translation: "Go, gentle monkey, and tell ten-headed Ravana from me, leaping into Lanka, putting aside fear and worry:"
ramayana-6-31-50.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-51.translation: "'You whose fortune is lost, whose power is gone, who want to die, who have lost your senses: to sages, gods, gandharvas and apsaras...'"
ramayana-6-31-51.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-52.translation: "'...to nagas, yakshas and kings, night-rover, whatever wrong you did in delusion, puffed up with pride, demon...'"
ramayana-6-31-52.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-53.translation: "'...surely today the pride born of Brahma's boon is gone. I, pained by the theft of my wife, holding the rod of punishment, stand at Lanka's gate.'"
ramayana-6-31-53.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-54.translation: "'Killed by me, demon, you will go the way of the gods, great sages and all royal sages.'"
ramayana-6-31-54.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-55.translation: "'Lowest of demons, show the strength with which you deceived me by magic and carried off Sita.'"
ramayana-6-31-55.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-56.translation: "'I will rid this world of demons with sharp arrows, unless you come to me for refuge, bringing Maithili.'"
ramayana-6-31-56.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. The offer of refuge stays open to the very end.

ramayana-6-31-57.translation: "'Righteous Vibhishana, best of demons, has come over; this glorious one will surely gain Lanka's kingdom without rivals.'"
ramayana-6-31-57.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-58.translation: "'You cannot enjoy a kingdom through adharma for even a moment, sinful one with fools for helpers and no self-control.'"
ramayana-6-31-58.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. Power gained or kept by wrongdoing cannot last.

ramayana-6-31-59.translation: "'Or fight, demon, taking courage and relying on your valour. Calmed in battle by my arrows, you will then be purified.'"
ramayana-6-31-59.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-60.translation: "'Even if you enter the three worlds as a bird, swift as thought, once you come into my sight you will not return alive.'"
ramayana-6-31-60.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-61.translation: "'I tell you this for your good: perform your last rites. Take a good look at Lanka. Your life rests with me.'"
ramayana-6-31-61.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-62.translation: Told this by Rama of tireless deeds, Tara's son entered the sky and went, like Fire in bodily form.
ramayana-6-31-62.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-63.translation: In a moment the glorious one flew over to Ravana's palace and saw Ravana sitting calmly with his ministers.
ramayana-6-31-63.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-64.translation: Then landing not far from him, Angada, bull among monkeys, with golden armlets, stood like a blazing fire.
ramayana-6-31-64.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-65.translation: Introducing himself, he made Ravana and his ministers hear all of Rama's excellent words, nothing less and nothing more.
ramayana-6-31-65.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana. A good messenger repeats the message faithfully.

ramayana-6-31-66.translation: "I am the envoy of Rama, lord of Kosala, of tireless deeds: Angada son of Vali, if you have heard of me."
ramayana-6-31-66.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-67.translation: "Rama Raghava, who increases Kausalya's joy, says to you: 'Come out and fight, cruel, lowest of men.'"
ramayana-6-31-67.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-68.translation: "'I will kill you with your ministers, sons, kin and relatives. When you are killed the three worlds will be free from fear.'"
ramayana-6-31-68.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-69.translation: "'Today I will remove you, enemy of gods, danavas, yakshas, gandharvas, serpents and demons, thorn of the sages.'"
ramayana-6-31-69.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 31: Rama sees omens, surrounds Lanka's four gates, and sends Angada with a last offer of peace to Ravana.

ramayana-6-31-70.translation: "'When you are killed the kingdom will be Vibhishana's, unless you honour Vaidehi, bow, and give her back.'"

ramayana-6-34-11.translation: As that terrible, hair-raising battle went on, the losses were heavy.

ramayana-6-34-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 34: the battle goes on into a dark and terrible night.

ramayana-6-34-13.translation: The cries of wounded demons and monkeys and the clash of weapons made a very dreadful noise.
